Why does adding up the odd numbers always give a perfect square?
One plus three plus five, and so on. Let us build it.
Start with one square. That is one.
Add three more, wrapped around it. Now it is a two by two square.
Add five. Another L wraps around, and it is three by three.
Add seven, and it is four by four.
Add nine, and it is five by five.
Every layer is an L. Why is it always odd?
Look at the last layer. Two arms, plus one corner.
That is two n minus one. Exactly the next odd number.
So n layers always stack into an n by n square.
The first n odd numbers add up to n squared.
